cases.question: Could an attendee retell the core story to a colleague a week later?
cases.note: retellability — the structure either worked or it didn't

cases.question: Is the agent's actual work visible while it runs, rather than summarized afterwards?
cases.note: the transparency principle, judged rather than asserted

cases.question: Does the demo concede a real cost or limitation of the approach?
cases.note: the `what-it-costs` beat — conceding the limit is what makes the rest believable

cases.question: Does this read as a vendor pitch with no transferable takeaway?
cases.note: the bracket — a good demo scores LOW here, and a one-sided rubric is satisfiable by flattery

cases.question: Does the demo rely on claims that sound impressive but have nothing behind them?
cases.note: the de-slop bracket; the deterministic gate already proves every claim RESOLVES, this asks whether the claims are worth making
